title: Gymnopedie No. 1
source: Mutopia Project, https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=37, typeset by Evin Robertson (Public Domain)

musicalLanguage.description: This Mutopia typeset of Satie's Gymnopedie No. 1 runs 47 measures at 60 BPM in 3/4 time with 282 notes, and the stated D major is confirmed by the content (statedKeyFit 0.744; the detected key matches exactly). The MIDI is the compact volta rendering: one statement of the theme plus both 8-measure alternative endings laid end to end. Four structural regions open at measures 1, 5, 19, and 32. The opening vamp occupies measures 1-4 — measures 1 and 3 are byte-identical (right hand D4+F#4 over left-hand G2 and B3), and measures 2, 4, and 12 share the companion sonority (C#4+F#4 over D2 and A3). A 13-note right-hand span covering measures 1-8 restates at measures 9-16 (moderate evidence, coverage 0.286), confirmed measure-by-measure: 5=13, 6=14, 7=15, 8=16. Implied Gmaj7 windows land at measures 7 and 15, the same relative position in each of those two phrases. Gated labels cover 21% of measures (Am, Am7, and Gmaj7 tying at 4% each); the rest did not clear the confidence gate, which is expected of this spare texture rather than evidence of silence.
musicalLanguage.structure: Four structural regions from the section-lens pass, with the strongest boundary opening at measure 32 (novelty 3.949). Measures 1-4 are the opening vamp; measures 5-18 carry the first melody statement (the right hand's high A5 arrives at measure 5); measures 19-31 are the contrasting middle (novelty 3.115). Measures 32-47 are the two alternative endings laid sequentially: a left-hand span at measures 35-39 restates at 43-47, measure 32 matches 40 byte-for-byte, and the Am7 cadence at measure 38 returns at measure 46. The first ending settles on a gated D-major window at measure 39; the second closes on a gated D-minor window at measure 47. The busiest bars are 37 and 45 (6 onsets each), sitting inside those two endings; the sparsest are the cadence bars 38, 39, 46, and 47.
keyMoments: Bar 1: the opening vamp (right hand D4+F#4 over left-hand G2 and B3) returns byte-identical at measure 3, then the companion chord occupies measures 2, 4, and 12 — this teaches the piece's central lesson: an unresolved, floating harmony can anchor the first page just by returning unchanged.

Bar 5: this measure opens the section lens's second structural region (novelty 0.786), is the right hand's highest pitch in the piece (A5), and matches measure 13 byte-for-byte — demonstrating that a new phrase can begin exactly where independent structural analysis detects a shift, not by coincidence.

Bars 7-8: this 2-measure unit recurs at measures 15-16, each bar independently confirmed byte-identical to its counterpart eight measures later, and measure 7 itself carries an implied Gmaj7 window — a technique for hearing repetition as matched pairs of bars rather than isolated moments.

The two alternative endings at measures 32-39 and 40-47 share their opening (32=40) and their Am7 cadence (38=46), so learning one ending's frame teaches both; the second ending then settles on a gated Dm window at measure 47 rather than the first ending's D-major window at measure 39.
teachingGoals: Practice the opening vamp at measures 1-4 as the piece's harmonic and rhythmic anchor, then recognize its return inside the first melody statement rather than relearning those chords.
Learn the right hand's measures 1-8 thoroughly, since they restate at measures 9-16 with 0.286 coverage — this is the most efficient place to invest practice time in this typeset.
Listen for the implied Gmaj7 window returning at measures 7 and 15, and develop the ear to recognize this color each time it reappears in the same relative position.

Recognize the two alternative endings at measures 32-39 and 40-47 as one frame with two closes — understanding that connection makes the cadence at measures 46-47 feel inevitable rather than arbitrary.
styleTips: Play extremely slowly and unhurried at the MIDI's 60 BPM — listen for the opening vamp's two alternating chords settling fully before the melody's A5 at measure 5.

Keep the seventh-chord texture soft and blended with generous pedal, but lift and change with the implied Gmaj7 arrivals at measures 7 and 15 — listen for the color shifting gently rather than accenting the change.
Never accent anything — let gravity do the work through the near-identical second phrase at measures 9-16; listen for it landing with the same weightless quality as measures 1-8.

Treat measures 40-47 as a memory of measures 32-39 returning with a different close — listen for the shared Am7 cadence at 38 and 46, then let the final Dm window at measure 47 settle rather than build toward an ending.
